newsitem.title: USA: Washington Mutual responds to Ahmanson.
newsitem.headline: Washington Mutual responds to Ahmanson.

text.p: Washington Mutual Savings Bank said Sunday the doubts raised by H.F. Ahmanson and Co regarding the company's ability to account its proposed acquisition of Great Western Financial Corp were "unfounded."

The company issued its statement in response to Ahmanson's announcement on Friday that it filed an amendment to its lawsuit against Great Western. Ahmanson's proposed amendment asked the court to compel Great Western to disclose the risks of not being able to pool on its ability to complete the deal.
But Washington Mutual on Sunday said the accounting has been deemed appropriate by both companies' accounting advisors, Deloitte & Touche and Price Waterhouse.

"Both accounting firms advised and continue to advise that, in their view, the proposed Washington Mutual/Great Western transaction is appropriately accounted for as a pooling of interests," the company said in its statement.

Ahmanson recently raised its hostile stock offer for Great Western to $6.68 billion. Washington Mutual reached a definitive agreement to buy Great Western on March 6 in a stock swap valued at $6.44 billion.
"We continue to believe that investors recognize the superiority of this friendly merger, and we remain confident that our merger will be completed on schedule," Washington Mutual said.
Ahmanson said Friday Great Western failed to disclose that it took certain actions last December that may create an obstacle to the merger's qualifying for pooling treatment.

The actions outlined by Ahmanson included modifications to Great Western's stock compensation and benefit plans that changed the equity interest of the voting stock as well as the granting of about 3.75 million stock options to its officers, directors and senior executives during 1996.

Ahmanson said that under accepted accounting practices, the changes in equity interest are "presumed" to have been made in contemplation of the merger with Washington Mutual. Evidence that Great Western was considering a merger at the time it made the changes in December could preclude the use of pooling, Ahmanson said.
Washington Mutual said Ahmanson's latest charges were a sign of "desperation."
"We believe that Ahmanson will not succeed with its continuous attempts to confuse investors and misrepresent our agreed transaction," the company said.
